strategy.summary: PR #130 adds coupon codes (src/coupons.js: SAVE10 10% off rounded down, TENOFF £10 off capped at the total, case/space-insensitive matching, UnknownCouponError for other codes), a bulk discount (src/pricing.js: 10+ items get 10% when larger than the 5% spend discount) and lets priceBasket take a coupon applied after the discount. Existing tests only cover the spend discount and a coupon-less basket; formatPence is a refactor already covered by test/format.test.js. The tests must prove each new rule at unit level with Vitest.
inScope: discountFor bulk rule and its interaction with the spend discount
couponDiscount for SAVE10, TENOFF, case/space matching and unknown codes
priceBasket with a coupon: order of application, result shape, cap at zero, refusal
outOfScope: formatPence: refactor with unchanged output, already asserted by test/format.test.js (positive, padded, negative)
Behaviour the PR didn't change (lineTotal validation, spend discount threshold)
assumptions: Code, README and PR description agree on every rule; tests assert the code's values
An empty-string or absent coupon means no coupon (code uses a truthy check); not tested as it is not described by the PR

acceptanceCriteria.text: A basket of 10 or more items (summed across lines) gets 10% off its subtotal, rounded down
A basket of fewer than 10 items gets no bulk discount
When both apply, the larger of the bulk and spend discounts is taken, not both
SAVE10 takes 10% off the total, rounded down
TENOFF takes £10 (1000p) off, never more than the total so the total never goes below zero
A coupon code is matched whatever its case and surrounding spaces
An unknown coupon code raises UnknownCouponError naming the code
priceBasket applies a coupon after the discount and reports the amount it took as `coupon`

review.standard: General: recognise the app's behaviour by its structure, not a message's wording; check only the part of the message the test controls (the name it submitted)
review.summary: The unknown-code assertions match the message's quote marks ('"SAVE20"', and '"NOPE"' at test/pricing.test.js:79), which are wording coupons.js writes, not the code the test submitted.
review.failureScenario: If UnknownCouponError's message is reworded to `Unknown coupon: SAVE20`, the error still names the code (AC7 holds), but both refusal tests fail. Asserting toContain('SAVE20') / toContain('NOPE') still proves AC7 and doesn't depend on the punctuation.
